title: Ensure SSH Protocol is set to 2
description: SSH supports both protocol 1 and 2. Protocol 1 is insecure and should be disabled.
remediation:
Edit /etc/ssh/sshd_config. Set: Protocol 2
Then run: sudo systemctl restart sshd

title: Ensure SSH MaxAuthTries is set to 4 or less
description: The MaxAuthTries parameter specifies the maximum number of authentication attempts permitted.
remediation:
Edit /etc/ssh/sshd_config. Set: MaxAuthTries 4
Then run: sudo systemctl restart sshd

title: Ensure SSH IgnoreRhosts is enabled
description: The IgnoreRhosts setting controls whether rhosts files are used.
remediation:
Edit /etc/ssh/sshd_config. Set: IgnoreRhosts yes
Then run: sudo systemctl restart sshd

title: Ensure SSH HostbasedAuthentication is disabled
description: HostbasedAuthentication should be disabled in favor of public key authentication.
remediation:
Edit /etc/ssh/sshd_config. Set: HostbasedAuthentication no
Then run: sudo systemctl restart sshd

title: Ensure SSH PermitRootLogin is disabled
description: Disallowing root logins via SSH requires attackers to authenticate as a regular user and then elevate to root.
remediation:
Edit /etc/ssh/sshd_config. Set: PermitRootLogin no
Then run: sudo systemctl restart sshd

title: Ensure SSH PermitEmptyPasswords is disabled
description: Empty password accounts are a security risk and should be prevented.
remediation:
Edit /etc/ssh/sshd_config. Set: PermitEmptyPasswords no
Then run: sudo systemctl restart sshd

title: Ensure SSH PermitUserEnvironment is disabled
description: The PermitUserEnvironment option allows users to set environment variables.
remediation:
Edit /etc/ssh/sshd_config. Set: PermitUserEnvironment no
Then run: sudo systemctl restart sshd

title: Ensure SSH X11Forwarding is disabled
description: X11Forwarding can allow attackers to gain screen access and potentially compromise account security.
remediation:
Edit /etc/ssh/sshd_config. Set: X11Forwarding no
Then run: sudo systemctl restart sshd

title: Ensure SSH MaxStartups is configured
description: The MaxStartups parameter limits concurrent unauthenticated connections.
remediation:
Edit /etc/ssh/sshd_config. Set: MaxStartups 10:30:60
Then run: sudo systemctl restart sshd

title: Ensure SSH MaxSessions is set to 10 or less
description: The MaxSessions parameter limits the number of open sessions per network connection.
remediation:
Edit /etc/ssh/sshd_config. Set: MaxSessions 10
Then run: sudo systemctl restart sshd

title: Ensure SSH LoginGraceTime is set to one minute or less
description: LoginGraceTime limits the time for successful authentication.
remediation:
Edit /etc/ssh/sshd_config. Set: LoginGraceTime 60
Then run: sudo systemctl restart sshd

title: Ensure SSH Banner is configured
description: The Banner option specifies a file with login banner text to display.
remediation:
Create /etc/ssh/banner.txt with login banner.
Edit /etc/ssh/sshd_config. Set: Banner /etc/ssh/banner.txt
Then run: sudo systemctl restart sshd

title: Ensure IP forwarding is disabled
description: IP forwarding allows the system to route packets between networks.
remediation: Set kernel parameter: net.ipv4.ip_forward = 0

title: Ensure ICMP redirects are not accepted
description: ICMP redirects allow attackers to redirect network traffic.
remediation: Set kernel parameters to disable ICMP redirects

title: Ensure TCP SYN Cookies is enabled
description: SYN cookies protect against SYN flood attacks.
remediation: Set kernel parameter: net.ipv4.tcp_syncookies = 1

title: Ensure mounting of cramfs filesystems is disabled
description: Uncommon filesystems should be disabled if not needed.
remediation: Run: echo 'install cramfs /bin/true' | sudo tee -a /etc/modprobe.d/cramfs.conf

title: Ensure password expiration is 365 days or less
description: Password expiration forces users to periodically change their passwords.
remediation: Edit /etc/login.defs. Set: PASS_MAX_DAYS 365

title: Ensure password creation requirements are configured
description: PAM should be configured to enforce strong password requirements.
remediation: Edit /etc/security/pwquality.conf. Configure password complexity requirements.

title: Ensure sudo is installed
description: sudo allows authorized users to execute commands as root.
remediation: Install sudo: sudo apt install sudo

title: Ensure sudo commands use pty
description: Running sudo through a pseudo-terminal (pty) improves session tracking.
remediation: Add to /etc/sudoers: Defaults use_pty

title: Ensure sudo log file exists
description: Sudo should log all commands to a file for auditing.
remediation: Add to /etc/sudoers: Defaults logfile='/var/log/sudo.log'

title: Ensure ufw is installed
description: ufw (Uncomplicated Firewall) simplifies firewall configuration.
remediation: Install ufw: sudo apt install ufw

title: Ensure ufw service is enabled
description: The ufw service should be enabled and running.
remediation: Enable and start ufw: sudo systemctl enable ufw && sudo systemctl start ufw

title: Ensure default deny firewall policy
description: Firewall default policies should be deny for incoming, forward, and allow for outgoing.
remediation: Configure firewall defaults: sudo ufw default deny incoming && sudo ufw default allow outgoing

title: Ensure SSH access is limited
description: SSH access should be restricted to specific users and groups.
remediation: Edit /etc/ssh/sshd_config. Configure: AllowUsers or AllowGroups

title: Ensure SSH LogLevel is appropriate
description: SSH LogLevel should be set to VERBOSE or higher.
remediation: Edit /etc/ssh/sshd_config. Set: LogLevel VERBOSE

title: Ensure xinetd is not installed
description: xinetd is a legacy network service and should be removed.
remediation: Remove xinetd: sudo apt purge xinetd

title: Ensure X11 Server is not installed
description: X11 should not be installed unless explicitly needed.
remediation: Remove X11: sudo apt purge xserver-xorg-*
